Yes. Hansen data detected **1.8 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2019**, about 0.05% of the property. The area was mapped as planted pine forest, not native forest, in Uruguay’s 2021 forest map.

An additional 3.1 hectares of loss was detected in patches smaller than 0.5 hectares; these were not counted as an event. The JRC map classified the entire 1.8-hectare event area as forest in 2020, so the loss does not necessarily indicate permanent deforestation.
